# TIFF Inspector regression fixtures

All files in this directory are generated by
`scripts/gen-fixtures/gen_fixtures.py` (Python 3.9+, standard library only).
The generator contains its own small TIFF writer, written independently of the
OCaml parser under test, and its output is deterministic (byte-identical on
every run).

## Regenerating

```sh
python3 scripts/gen-fixtures/gen_fixtures.py test/fixtures            # write
python3 scripts/gen-fixtures/gen_fixtures.py test/fixtures --verify   # write + self-check
```

`--verify` re-reads every fixture with a second, independent minimal reader
in the same script, then checks the values documented below: header, IFD
count, dimensions, samples, bits, SampleFormat, photometric, planar
configuration, compression, strip/tile counts and bounds, and that deflate
data decompresses. It also checks the expected failure category for each
malformed file. The script exits non-zero if any check fails. Commit the
regenerated `.tif` files together with any change to the generator.

## Writer conventions

- Entries are sorted by tag. Values that fit in the value field (4 bytes for
  classic TIFF, 8 for BigTIFF) are stored inline, left-justified and
  zero-padded. Larger values go right after their IFD.
- File layout per IFD: pixel chunks, then the IFD, then out-of-line values.
  Each item starts on a 4-byte boundary (classic) or an 8-byte boundary
  (BigTIFF), so the first strip always starts at offset 8 (classic) or 16
  (BigTIFF).
- ImageWidth/ImageLength/RowsPerStrip/TileWidth/TileLength are SHORT.
  StripOffsets/StripByteCounts/TileOffsets/TileByteCounts are LONG (LONG8 in
  BigTIFF).
- Pixel data is a deterministic byte pattern. Pixel values carry no meaning.

## Well-formed fixtures

Legend: spp = SamplesPerPixel; SF = SampleFormat tag value ("absent" means
the tag is not present, so readers should default to 1 = unsigned int);
PC = PlanarConfiguration ("absent" means the default, 1 = chunky);
Comp = Compression.

| File | Bytes | Purpose | BO | Format | IFDs |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| `gray8.tif` | 332 | Baseline grayscale; defaults for missing SampleFormat/PlanarConfiguration; RATIONAL + ASCII tags | II | classic | 1 |
| `rgb_contig.tif` | 482 | Chunky RGB, multiple strips, multi-value BitsPerSample/SampleFormat stored at offset | II | classic | 1 |
| `rgb_planar.tif` | 486 | Big-endian, planar (separate) RGB, one strip per plane | MM | classic | 1 |
| `float32_sampleformat_offset.tif` | 354 | **Regression:** SampleFormat=[3,3,3] read from an offset (not inline) | II | classic | 1 |
| `multi_ifd.tif` | 466 | IFD chain of 3 directories with different shapes | II | classic | 3 |
| `deflate.tif` | 206 | Adobe Deflate (8) compression, Predictor=1 | II | classic | 1 |
| `bigtiff.tif` | 360 | BigTIFF (magic 43), 16-bit, LONG8 strip offsets/counts | II | BigTIFF | 1 |
| `bigtiff_rgb_inline.tif` | 300 | **Regression:** BigTIFF RGB with BitsPerSample=[8,8,8] and SampleFormat=[1,1,1] inline in the 8-byte value field (as GDAL writes them) | II | BigTIFF | 1 |
| `tiled.tif` | 1192 | Tiled layout (TileOffsets/TileByteCounts), no strip tags | II | classic | 1 |
| `gray_alpha.tif` | 166 | **Regression:** multi-value inline tag (BitsPerSample=[8,8] in the 4-byte field), ExtraSamples | II | classic | 1 |
| `unknown_tag.tif` | 776 | Private tags 65000 (ASCII) and 65001 (100 LONGs at offset): unknown-tag display and value truncation | II | classic | 1 |

Other documented values:

- `gray8.tif`, `unknown_tag.tif`: ImageDescription = `"gray8 fixture"`,
  XResolution = YResolution = 72/1, ResolutionUnit = 2 (inch).
- `gray_alpha.tif`: ExtraSamples = [2] (unassociated alpha).
- `unknown_tag.tif`: tag 65000 ASCII `"hello private tag"` (18 bytes with
  NUL), tag 65001 LONG count 100 = 0..99. An inspector with a per-tag value
  limit below 100 should report this tag as truncated.

## Malformed fixtures

| File | Bytes | Construction | Expected result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `empty.tif` | 0 | Empty file | `not_a_tiff` ("The file is empty") |
| `not_a_tiff.tif` | 24 | PNG signature `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` + 16 bytes | `not_a_tiff` |
| `bad_magic.tif` | 16 | `II`, magic 99, offset 8, zero padding | `not_a_tiff` |
| `truncated_header.tif` | 5 | First 5 bytes of `gray8.tif` | `truncated` |
| `ifd_offset_out_of_range.tif` | 16 | Valid `II*\0` header, first IFD offset 0x7FFFFFF0 | `malformed` (IFD offset points outside the file) |
| `truncated_ifd.tif` | 180 | `gray8.tif` cut at IFD offset 136 + 2 + 3×12 + 6, in the middle of entry 4 | `truncated` |
| `strip_out_of_bounds.tif` | 332 | `gray8.tif` with StripByteCounts = 65536; strip at offset 8, so 8 + 65536 > 332 | succeeds (1 IFD, header values as in gray8) with directory warning `chunk_out_of_bounds` |
| `ifd_loop.tif` | 332 | `gray8.tif` with its next-IFD pointer set to its own IFD offset (136) | succeeds with 1 IFD; `ifd_walk.status` = `failed` (loop detected) and file warning `ifd_walk_failed` |
| `unknown_field_type.tif` | 344 | `gray8.tif` + entry tag 65002, field type 99, count 1, value bytes `01 02 03 04` | `unsupported_feature`, fatal: ocaml-tiff rejects the whole directory when an entry has an unknown field type (see limitations), so the inspector fails with exit code 1 and names the tag and type |
| `huge_strip_count.tif` | 332 | `gray8.tif` with StripOffsets = LONG, count 0x3FFFFFFF, value offset 8 (StripByteCounts still has count 1) | `malformed` ("declares 1073741823 values, more than the file could contain"): rejected by the inspector's preflight before ocaml-tiff allocates the ~4 GiB buffer. A `truncated` or out-of-memory result would be a regression |

Expected categories above are asserted by `test/unit/test_inspect.ml`; the full
output is pinned by the golden files in `test/golden/`.

## Adding a fixture

1. In `build_fixtures()` in `scripts/gen-fixtures/gen_fixtures.py`, add an
   entry `fx["name.tif"] = write_tiff([Page([...tags...], [chunks])], ...)[0]`.
   - Use `Tag(tag, TYPE, values)`. Pass `OFFSETS` / `COUNTS` as the values of
     the offsets/bytecounts tags and the writer fills them in.
   - Use `RawTag(tag, type_code, count, value_field_bytes)` for deliberately
     invalid entries.
   - `write_tiff(..., little_endian=False)` writes MM;
     `write_tiff(..., bigtiff=True)` writes BigTIFF.
     `Page(..., next_override="self" | offset)` corrupts the IFD chain.
   - Keep files small (under 4 KB).
2. Add the expected values to `EXPECTED` (well-formed) or `EXPECTED_ERRORS`
   (malformed) in the same script, or add a dedicated check in `verify()`.
3. Document the fixture in this file.
4. Run the generator with `--verify`, run it a second time, and confirm the
   sha256 hashes are unchanged.
